    tsflow

    tsflow defines and runs declarative time-series pipelines.

    The current MVP contract is:

    • raw series are injected at runtime as named ts objects
    • derived series are evaluated as ordered pipeline steps
    • transforms resolve as ordinary R functions
    • YAML is the canonical structured pipeline shape
    • CSV plus a sibling sidecar YAML file is a supported authoring convenience

    CSV Workflow

    The main spreadsheet-style format is:

    name,input,step_1,step_2,...

    Each step column is interpreted left to right as a pipe step. A sibling sidecar file with the same stem can provide shared values:

    • pipeline.csv
    • pipeline.meta.yml

    The sidecar may define:

    • vars
    • outputs
    • metadata

    CSV step cells can reference sidecar vars with @name.

    Example CSV:

    name,input,step_1,step_2
gdp.nominal.quarterly,gdp.nominal.quarterly.sa,"jsa(gdp.nominal.annual.nsa, method=@jsa_method)",
construction.deflator.quarterly,construction.nominal.quarterly,div(construction.real.quarterly),mul(100)

    Example sidecar:

    vars:
  jsa_method: denton-cholette
  base_year: 2021
  conversion: sum

    YAML remains the canonical structured shape. CSV is compiled into the same internal step representation before normalization, validation, DAG planning, and execution.

    Plan Then Execute

    Plan the pipeline first:

    plan <- plan_pipeline(
  path = "inst/examples/gdp_construction.csv",
  transform_env = environment()
)

plan
dag_edges(plan$dag, include_labels = TRUE)

    Then execute it with injected inputs:

    data("gdp_construction_inputs", package = "tsflow")

result <- execute_pipeline(
  path = "inst/examples/gdp_construction.csv",
  inputs = gdp_construction_inputs,
  transform_env = environment()
)

    result$values contains the full executed state. By default, result$outputs contains derived series only. Pass outputs = ... to execute and materialize only the upstream subgraph needed for one or more targets.

    In interactive sessions, execution shows a progress bar automatically when progressr is installed. Existing user handlers are respected, and progress can be disabled with progress = FALSE or options(tsflow.progress = FALSE).

    If future and future.apply are installed, independent DAG frontiers can be executed using the current future::plan(). The plan controls the actual parallel backend and worker count:

    future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 2)

result <- execute_pipeline(
  path = "inst/examples/gdp_construction.csv",
  inputs = gdp_construction_inputs,
  transform_env = environment(),
  outputs = "construction.nominal.quarterly"
)

    Transforms can be referenced as bare names such as jsa or namespaced functions such as stats::lag. Bare names are resolved from transform_env; namespaced functions are resolved directly from the package namespace.

    Execution Semantics

    • result$values contains the full executed state for the run.
    • result$outputs contains the materialized user-facing outputs.
    • If outputs = NULL, result$outputs defaults to derived series only.
    • If outputs = ... is provided, execution is pruned to the upstream subgraph needed for those targets.
    • If future and future.apply are available, parallel frontier execution is enabled by the current future::plan().
    • The actual parallel backend and worker count are controlled entirely by that future::plan().

    DAG Inspection

    Planning produces a dependency DAG. Useful helpers include:

    • dag_edges()
    • upstream_nodes()
    • downstream_nodes()
    • dag_to_igraph()
    • dag_to_visnetwork()

    For interactive inspection in HTML output, use dag_to_visnetwork(). The packaged vignette shows that workflow with a fixed left-to-right layout. Clicking a node highlights the upstream calculation path used to produce it and fades unrelated nodes. The widget also shows the selected node and its upstream path in an on-page details panel.

    Example Files

    The package includes:

    • inst/examples/gdp_construction.csv
    • inst/examples/gdp_construction.meta.yml
    • vignettes/gdp-construction.Rmd

    The vignette is the best end-to-end walkthrough.
